overall_reason: The invoice-and-deposit story is there, but the ground, invoice and deposit card are all one orange family, so the deposit card sinks into the invoice.

score.reason: T-SIGNATURE and T-BOLD-MOVE fail: the invoice ground #ecac84, deposit card #e29b7c and frame orange sit within one value band, with #813d31 text everywhere.

findings.evidence: The deposit card (#e29b7c) is darker than the invoice it sits on (#ecac84) and close to the orange frame, so the newest information reads as a shadow.
findings.before: Deposit card in the same orange as its surroundings
findings.after: Give the deposit card its own material, lighter and neutral, above the invoice
findings.why: The deposit is the news in this scene; when it sinks, the composition has no subject.

findings.evidence: Frame, invoice and card all use orange grounds with the same #813d31 ink; 'Paid' and 'Arriving tomorrow' get no contrast of their own.
findings.after: Spend the colour in one place, for example the paid status, and keep the layers neutral
findings.why: With the colour everywhere, no element is louder than the rest.

strengths: The layered invoice and deposit arrangement is a sound idea worth keeping.
not_investigated: 00-contract.md is absent: no brand authority, audience or overrides were available, so the item was read as an Operate composition (CON-018).
T-RIVAL-NAME cap: the composition names no client, so every placeholder label holds under any rival; the cap at 5 was not applied and the test was used only to spot default copy.
T-IDEA-CARRIES: single composition, there is no second screen to carry the idea.
T-DELETE-PICTURE and T-PROMISE-PICTURED: no lead image and no marketing promise, except where a finding says so.
T-COVER-TEXT: no brand theme or motif to recognise.
The caption above some frames ('Considered composition' / 'Composition problem') is fixture text from the capture host and was not judged.
